title: Salesforce Test Drive Catalog (test-drives.json)
description: Contribution-safety grammar for the test-drive catalog. Product teams add one entry per test drive. Entries are strict (additionalProperties: false) so a typo'd field is caught at authoring time rather than silently ignored by the engine; extend the contract by PR to this schema, the same way the skills model vocabulary is extended. The root stays open so catalog-level metadata can be added over time. Value-level policy that a JSON Schema cannot express (prompt file exists on disk, orderedSkills name real skills provided by salesforce-development or a requires.plugins plugin, requires.plugins name real marketplace plugins, owner contact is reachable) is intended to live in a future imperative lint gate — see AUTHORING.md.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier. Used for direct launch (/salesforce-test-drive:start <id>) and as the default promptPath stem. Must be unique within the catalog.

title.description: Menu label shown to the user, e.g. 'Service help agent (website chat widget)'.

description.description: One-line, chooser-facing summary of what this drive builds and the end result.

owner.description: The product team that owns this drive's prompt and manifest. The framework owns the engine; the owning team owns whether their prompt sings.

contact.description: A durable contact — a Slack channel, email alias, or GUS team — not an individual.

requires.description: What the connected org must satisfy for this drive to succeed. The engine gates on this in Step 4 and surfaces gaps as actionable feedback.

licenses.description: License names the org must have (e.g. an Agentforce/Einstein license).

userPerms.description: User permissions the running user needs.

orgPerms.description: Org permissions/preferences that must be enabled.

provisioningTier.description: Which provisioning path satisfies this drive, so the engine can route a user with no org: 'any' = any authenticated org; 'developer-edition' = a full Developer Edition org; 'agentforce' = an Agentforce-enabled org (e.g. free Agentforce Developer Edition).

plugins.description: Marketplace plugin ids this drive needs installed BEYOND the base 'salesforce-development' companion (which every drive requires and the engine verifies in Step 0). Example: 'agentforce-adlc', which ships the Agentforce authoring skills (agentforce-generate) — these are NOT part of salesforce-development. The engine checks each id is installed at the top of Step 4; if one is missing it routes into the companion's confirm-then-install (Dynamic Plugin Loading) flow rather than hard-stopping, then has the user run /reload-plugins and re-run. Each name must match a plugin in the Salesforce marketplace catalog.

orderedSkills.description: The skills this drive choreographs, in build order — provided either by the base 'salesforce-development' companion or by a plugin declared in requires.plugins (e.g. agentforce-generate comes from agentforce-adlc). Advisory for the engine and reviewers; the prompt is the source of truth for execution.

presetInputs.description: Plumbing answers the engine injects so the run doesn't stall on mechanical setup (output paths, naming defaults). Do NOT pre-answer the target org here: the engine targets the org it settled on during readiness (the user's default org, under whatever alias THEY use), so a hardcoded org alias would misfire for anyone whose org isn't named that. And do NOT pre-answer showcase design questions — live collaboration on those is the demo.

promptPath.description: Path to the steel-thread prompt, relative to the plugin's prompts/ directory, e.g. 'service-help-agent.md'.

handoff.description: Scripted next-step shown when the build finishes — how the user sees the result work (e.g. 'Open your org, go to the chat widget, and ask it a question'). Use `<angle-bracket>` placeholders for values the engine resolves at handoff time: `<targetOrg>` (the alias/username of the org it settled on); `<projectDir>` (the absolute path of the DX project the build scaffolded/used — prefix any directory-sensitive command with `cd <projectDir> && …` since the build often scaffolds a nested, drive-named project); and, for values the build produces, a descriptive token such as `<agentApiName>` (the created agent's API name). Match commands to the lifecycle state the engine leaves the build in — the engine is draft-first (deploys but never publishes/activates), so an Agentforce preview must use `--authoring-bundle <agentApiName>`, not `--api-name` (which only resolves for a published+activated agent and fails on a draft with `SingleRecordQuery_NoRecords`). The engine substitutes every placeholder before showing the command, so it's copy-pasteable against the user's org. Never hardcode an org alias, and never leave a value the engine can't resolve as a bare `<…>` token — unresolved angle brackets paste into a shell as redirection and fail.
